result.title: Perception into Imagination: Executable Memory for World Models
result.summary: Physical agents must use what they previously saw or touched after visibility or contact is lost. Their actions change the implications of these remembered facts. We introduce executable perceptual memory (EPM), a world-model framework that advances explicit perceptual state alongside neural latent dynamics during imagination. Its evolving read-out informs reward prediction, value estimation and policy learning. We align reward inputs with the transitions that produced them and supervise the reward head on open-loop rollouts of recorded actions. On Memory Maze $13\times13$, EPM reaches 30.37 return at 1M interactions, compared with 23.37 when the same evolving read-out informs only policy and value on a common perceptual front end: a gain of 7.00 [3.80, 10.21]. The complete method also improves control on $9\times9$ and in MiniWorld. Probes of remembered, out-of-view arrivals show stronger reward anticipation in both visual implementations. Concentration, tactile recovery and real tactile frames demonstrate complementary roles of remembered facts in imagined-policy training, motion-dependent decisions and sensory-content retention. EPM connects persistent perception to the predicted consequences and learning signals of a world model for Physical AI.

AI.brief_summary: 提出「可执行感知记忆」(EPM) 世界模型框架：在想象/开环 rollout 中让显式感知状态与神经 latent dynamics 并行演化，其读出用于奖励预测、价值估计与策略学习，并在 Memory Maze 与 MiniWorld 上验证控制收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 显式记忆状态与 latent 动态并行、读出驱动下游预测，以及把奖励输入对齐到产生它的转移并在开环 rollout 上监督读出，可能为 LVR 中「内部状态是否保留视外视觉细节」与轨迹监督/贡献分配提供核查线索，但属 RL 世界模型，迁移价值待判断。
